title: Constitutionality of Race-Based Department of Education Programs
publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Legal Counsel
summary: Office of Legal Counsel memorandum opinion for the Acting General Counsel of the Department of Education. It examines Higher Education Act programmes for Hispanic-serving and other minority-serving institutions and states, programme by programme, which the Office considers unconstitutional and whether the provision is severable. It says it does not address programmes for historically Black or tribally controlled colleges.
why_it_mattered: The Office of Legal Counsel opinion of December 2025 on the Education Department's programmes for designated institutions. The Department's decisions to stop awarding under several of those programmes are read against it; it is an executive-branch opinion and not a court ruling.
key_facts: Dated December 2, 2025; addressed to the Acting General Counsel, Department of Education.
Developing Hispanic-Serving Institutions (20 U.S.C. 1101b(a)), PPOHA (20 U.S.C. 1102a(b)(1)) and HSI STEM (20 U.S.C. 1101(b), 1067q(b)(2)(B)) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.

Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian-Serving Institutions (20 U.S.C. 1059d), Native American-Serving Nontribal Institutions (20 U.S.C. 1059f(a)), AANAPISI (20 U.S.C. 1059g(a)) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.
Native Hawaiian Career and Technical Education (20 U.S.C. 2326(h)) - concluded unconstitutional.
Predominantly Black Institutions formula grants (20 U.S.C. 1059e) - concluded unconstitutional and inseverable.
Predominantly Black Institutions competitive grants (20 U.S.C. 1067q) - concluded unconstitutional but severable; grants may continue without regard to whether the recipient is a PBI.
Minority Science and Engineering Improvement (20 U.S.C. 1067a(b)) - concluded unconstitutional but severable; grants may continue without regard to whether the recipient is a minority institution.
McNair programme - partially unconstitutional, severable; Student Support Services - may be administered.
The opinion says it does not opine on HBCU or tribally controlled college programmes.
quotes: Certain race-based grant programs administered by the Department of Education violate the Fifth Amendment's equal-protection component.
We were not asked to, and therefore do not, opine on programs involving Historically Black Colleges and Universities
